fail_closed_rules: Green Belt designation does not itself determine planning permission and Green Belt is not a landscape-quality designation
grey belt identification does not automatically mean allocation, release or approval
grey belt must be assessed under the current NPPF definition and relevant footnote-7 exclusions; generic brownfield status is insufficient
a Green Belt annual-return polygon is a snapshot and may not reflect boundary changes adopted after the return date
Green Belt core grouping is an analytical/category layer and is not a legal parcel boundary or development consent
Green Belt statistics are aggregate evidence and cannot establish parcel-level designation without current spatial evidence
Local Green Space designation is plan-led and zero Planning Data records/providers does not mean no Local Green Space exists
open-space need or accessible-greenspace proximity standards do not create a planning permission or legal access right
National Landscape is a non-statutory rebrand; the statutory designation remains Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty
Protected Landscapes duty requires relevant authorities to seek to further statutory purposes but does not itself create an automatic refusal
Protected Landscape management plans are strategic/material evidence and are not themselves the statutory development plan
a National Park/National Landscape boundary does not prove ownership, public access or development prohibition
development outside a Protected Landscape boundary may affect its setting; outside-boundary status is not a no-impact finding
major development in a Protected Landscape requires proposal-specific policy assessment; designation alone is not the final decision
Heritage Coast is defined by agreement rather than statutory designation and must not be treated as an AONB/National Park legal boundary
National Character Areas and landscape character assessments describe character and evidence; they are not consent boundaries
landscape sensitivity/capacity evidence is scenario- and scale-dependent and does not equal a parcel-level permission outcome
CRoW access land/public-access mapping does not establish ownership, unrestricted access in every circumstance or development rights
Green Infrastructure and accessible-greenspace datasets are analytical/planning evidence and not legal designations unless separately designated
